The bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to establish criteria for qualified primary care providers serving as primary care medical homes. Beginning no later than January 1, 2027, $5,000,000 annually shall be used to obtain federal financial participation to pay a monthly per‑member fee of not less than $75 to such DHHS‑qualified providers; any remaining funds are to be transferred to the medical assistance program and the Children's Health Insurance Program. Use of these funds requires applicable federal approvals. DHHS is authorized to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations necessary to implement the Medicaid Access and Quality Act.

Highlights affecting the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS):

- Establishes the "Medicaid Access and Quality Act" and directs DHHS to set criteria for qualified primary care providers to serve as primary care medical homes.  
- Requires DHHS to adopt rules and regulations necessary to implement the Act.  
- Funding: beginning no later than Jan 1, 2027, $5 million annually will be used to draw federal financial participation to pay a monthly per-member fee of at least $75 to qualifying primary care providers (target populations). Any remaining funds will be transferred to the Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP).  
- Use of funds is subject to required federal approvals. Legislature intends Medicaid practitioner fee schedule rates and related General Fund appropriations not be reduced below July 1, 2024 levels.

Defines "department" as the Department of Economic Development and assigns it authority to establish a grant program to procure annual licenses for preexisting three‑dimensional, game‑based learning platforms for middle and high schools. The department must develop application/prioritization criteria, accept developer applications, and may adopt rules. Grants funded with lottery funds pursuant to section 79‑3501 shall be awarded from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund (administered by the State Department of Education); grant funds may be used only to procure licenses (not for R&D). Grantees must provide access to all Nebraska school districts; awards must be made by July 1 annually. The Department of Economic Development must file an annual report to the Clerk of the Legislature by December 1. The statute allocates 8.75% of the ten percent lottery transfer to these subsection (2) grants.
Additions: Key additions affecting the Department of Economic Development (DED): - "Department" is defined as the Department of Economic Development. - DED may approve grant applications for learning platforms, but grant funds may only be used to procure or purchase an annual license for a preexisting platf… 
Key additions affecting the Department of Economic Development (DED):

- "Department" is defined as the Department of Economic Development.  
- DED may approve grant applications for learning platforms, but grant funds may only be used to procure or purchase an annual license for a preexisting platform (not for R&D).  
- Eligible platforms must align academic content with State Board of Education standards (high school and equivalent middle‑school standards), comply with ISO 27001, and demonstrate statewide implementation experience.  
- Approved grants authorized by DED will be awarded from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund administered by the State Department of Education.

No new appropriations or budget line‑item changes are specified; funding is to come from the existing SDE Improvement Grant Fund.

Summary: LB529 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §73-803 (State Procurement Act) to revise definitions used in state contracting. It specifies "Division" as the materiel division of the Department of Administrative Services and alters the definition of "state agency" for procurement of services to exclude the University of Nebraska, Nebraska state colleges, the Nebraska Investment Council, the courts, the Legislature, and any officer or state agency established by t… 
LB529 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §73-803 (State Procurement Act) to revise definitions used in state contracting. It specifies "Division" as the materiel division of the Department of Administrative Services and alters the definition of "state agency" for procurement of services to exclude the University of Nebraska, Nebraska state colleges, the Nebraska Investment Council, the courts, the Legislature, and any officer or state agency established by the Nebraska Constitution. The change is to apply to actions taken on or after July 19, 2024. The bill repeals the original section and contains an emergency clause making it effective upon passage. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.

Summary: LB52 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-1850 to revise victim‑notification duties involving the Department of Correctional Services (DOCS) and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). LB52 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-1850 to revise victim‑notification duties involving the Department of Correctional Services (DOCS) and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). Key provisions: county attorneys must forward victim names/addresses to DOCS and DHHS; DOCS must include victim names in offender files (not public) and notify victims of furloughs/releases/transfers, escapes and returns, discharge (30 days’ notice when practicable), participation in community programs, earliest parole/release date calculations, sentence reductions, and victims’ rights to submit statements; DOCS must forward victim contact information to DHHS when a commitment petition is filed; DHHS must notify victims regarding commitment petitions, escapes/returns, discharges/changes in disposition, furloughs/releases of 24+ hours, and entry/termination of release programs. DOCS and DHHS must adopt rules to implement these duties. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.

109-1-LB530_FinalPassedLegislature 109, Session 1 (2025)LB530_Final_Copy.docxDOCXDepartment of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Transportation
Summary: The bill affects five agencies as follows: - DHHS: Peace officers delivering juveniles under custody or mental‑health holds must turn custody to DHHS, which must make and supervise temporary placements (ending after 48 hours if no court order) and may consent to emergency medical/psychological treatment; officers must forward mental‑health certificates to county attorneys and notify parents. DHHS must also receive sealing notices when it was a p… 
The bill affects five agencies as follows:

- DHHS: Peace officers delivering juveniles under custody or mental‑health holds must turn custody to DHHS, which must make and supervise temporary placements (ending after 48 hours if no court order) and may consent to emergency medical/psychological treatment; officers must forward mental‑health certificates to county attorneys and notify parents. DHHS must also receive sealing notices when it was a party or the juvenile was a ward and may access/release sealed juvenile records for intake, case plans, evaluations, federal reporting, supervision/protection, and licensing/certification duties.

- DCS: Bars placement/transfer of specified juveniles to adult correctional facilities or the secure youth confinement facility and excludes DCS institutions from the definition of staff‑secure juvenile facilities; DCS may access sealed juvenile records for individuals under its care for supervision and investigations.

- DMV: Courts must transmit abstracts/notice to the DMV when juvenile licenses are impounded, juveniles are prohibited from obtaining permits, or a sealing order includes such restrictions.

- DOT: Authorizes temporary reductions of posted highway speeds for visibility, traction, emergencies or congestion with required electronic signage, policy, records, 5‑mph increment guidance, and rulemaking; DOT must erect/maintain Move‑Over/stopped‑vehicle signs and may treat DOT agents as road‑assistance personnel.

- Department of Labor: Must provide a website link informing employers they may not ask about sealed records and that applications should state applicants need not disclose sealed records.

Funding: Probation fees are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Probation Program Cash Fund.
Additions: - Department of Transportation: Expanded authority to temporarily reduce posted maximum speeds for weather, traction, emergencies or congestion; required use of electronic/digital signs, five‑mph increment changes, no minimum speed during reductions, recordkeeping and policy development duties, and… 
- Department of Transportation: Expanded authority to temporarily reduce posted maximum speeds for weather, traction, emergencies or congestion; required use of electronic/digital signs, five‑mph increment changes, no minimum speed during reductions, recordkeeping and policy development duties, and rulemaking authority. Also adds safe‑passing rules for stopped vehicles and vulnerable road users, and a prima facie reckless‑driving standard for speeds over double the limit; repeat violations carry Class IIIA misdemeanor exposure.

- Department of Motor Vehicles: Courts may suspend (up to 2 years) or revoke (15 years for more serious offenses) operator’s licenses as part of convictions for intentionally tampering with electronic monitoring devices.

- Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Labor: No substantive agency‑specific duties or budgetary/funding or appropriation changes identified in the added text.

109-1-LB532_IntroGeneral FileLegislature 109, Session 1 (2025)LB532_Intro_Copy.docxDOCXDepartment of Labor
Summary: The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Labor and assigns enforcement duties to the Commissioner of Labor and the Department of Labor. The commissioner may determine employer violations, notify employers (15 working days to contest), provide hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act, and notify licensing agencies of final violations. Licensing suspensions must occur within 72 hours; reinstatement requires demonstrating terminatio… 
The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Labor and assigns enforcement duties to the Commissioner of Labor and the Department of Labor. The commissioner may determine employer violations, notify employers (15 working days to contest), provide hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act, and notify licensing agencies of final violations. Licensing suspensions must occur within 72 hours; reinstatement requires demonstrating termination of unauthorized workers and payment of a reinstatement fee equal to the greater of the commission’s investigative/enforcement costs or $1,000. For violations involving five or more unauthorized aliens, the commissioner imposes an additional 7–30 day suspension; repeat violations carry increased discipline. The Department must maintain a public violations database and may adopt rules. No appropriations or other budget allocations are included.
Additions: The added language designates "Department" as the Department of Labor and gives its commissioner enforcement duties: determine employer violations for hiring unauthorized aliens, notify employers (15 working days to contest with an APA hearing), and, after final determination, notify licensing agenc… 
The added language designates "Department" as the Department of Labor and gives its commissioner enforcement duties: determine employer violations for hiring unauthorized aliens, notify employers (15 working days to contest with an APA hearing), and, after final determination, notify licensing agencies to suspend licenses within 72 hours. Reinstatement requires the employer to (1) show the unauthorized worker was terminated and (2) pay a reinstatement fee to the commission equal to its investigation/enforcement costs or $1,000, whichever is greater; violations involving five or more unauthorized aliens carry an additional 7–30 day suspension. The Department must maintain a public violations database on its website and may adopt rules to implement the sections. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.

Summary: LB533 amends the Pharmacy Benefit Manager Licensure and Regulation Act. It defines “clinician‑administered drug” and requires specialty pharmacies that ship such drugs to comply with federal shipping standards (including USP general chapter 800), Drug Supply Chain Security Act track‑and‑trace rules, provide 24/7 access to an employed pharmacist or nurse, require five business‑day delivery notice to providers, and obtain provider signatures on del… 
LB533 amends the Pharmacy Benefit Manager Licensure and Regulation Act. It defines “clinician‑administered drug” and requires specialty pharmacies that ship such drugs to comply with federal shipping standards (including USP general chapter 800), Drug Supply Chain Security Act track‑and‑trace rules, provide 24/7 access to an employed pharmacist or nurse, require five business‑day delivery notice to providers, and obtain provider signatures on delivery. The bill requires pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and health carriers to establish appeal/exception processes for mandated specialty‑pharmacy dispensing and prohibits requiring patient pickup for provider administration. The statute identifies “Director” as the Director of Insurance (Nebraska Department of Insurance). Operative date: January 1, 2026. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
Additions: Adds duties for specialty pharmacies and obligations for pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and health carriers. Key government references: requires compliance with federal drug-shipment law including United States Pharmacopeia general chapter 800 and the federal Drug Supply Chain Security Act (21 U.S… 
Adds duties for specialty pharmacies and obligations for pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and health carriers. Key government references: requires compliance with federal drug-shipment law including United States Pharmacopeia general chapter 800 and the federal Drug Supply Chain Security Act (21 U.S.C. 360eee et seq.) (track-and-trace). Requirements include 24/7 access to a pharmacist or nurse, honoring refill requests per PBM/health carrier utilization procedures, five business‑day advance delivery notice and signature on receipt for shipments to providers, and adherence to DSCSA for compounded/manipulated clinician‑administered drugs. PBMs/health carriers must provide an appeal/exception process for delivery failures or urgent one‑time use. Prohibits forcing pharmacies to send clinician‑administered drugs to patients for patient transport to providers. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes.

Creates the Manufacturing Modernization Pilot Investment Act and designates the Department of Economic Development as the administering agency. The Department will: accept applications Oct 1–Nov 1, 2025; review them in receipt order; approve eligible projects subject to available funding; issue grants from a new Manufacturing Modernization Pilot Investment Fund (grants up to $250,000 each). LB537 directs the Department of Labor to administer the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund and to provide workforce development grants. The department must award grants evenly across the three congressional districts. Grants are to be used for developing job skills, money management, communication skills, job preparation, and job placement. Applicants must demonstrate one-to-one private fund matching, and grant recipients must report to the Department of Labor on job placement and self‑sufficiency outcomes. The Legislature intends to transfer $1,500,000 from the General Fund to the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 for the department to provide these grants.

109-1-LB539_IntroIndefinitely postponedLegislature 109, Session 1 (2025)LB539_Intro_Copy.docxDOCX
Summary: LB539 revises Nebraska handgun statutes and narrows roles for state and local law enforcement in background checks. The Nebraska State Patrol (NSP) is limited to receiving and furnishing only information necessary to determine eligibility for concealed-carry permits or handgun possession, must update/correct data made available to the federal NICS, and may only notify an applicant’s chief of police or county sheriff whether the applicant is disqu… 
LB539 revises Nebraska handgun statutes and narrows roles for state and local law enforcement in background checks. The Nebraska State Patrol (NSP) is limited to receiving and furnishing only information necessary to determine eligibility for concealed-carry permits or handgun possession, must update/correct data made available to the federal NICS, and may only notify an applicant’s chief of police or county sheriff whether the applicant is disqualified. Good-faith reporters (including mental health boards) are granted immunity. Intentionally inducing the NSP to request background information without reasonable belief of a valid application is a Class II misdemeanor. Licensed federal firearms importers/manufacturers/dealers must inspect required certificates and photo ID; false statements in such transfers are a Class IV felony. Several related statutory sections are repealed. No appropriations or funding changes are included.
Additions: Adds that criminal history record checks for firearms or explosives purposes apply to persons qualified for a concealed‑handgun permit under statute 69‑2430 or otherwise subject to statutory criminal history checks. Summary: Defines "Department" as the Department of Agriculture and "Director" as the Director of Agriculture (or designated representative). Defines "Department" as the Department of Agriculture and "Director" as the Director of Agriculture (or designated representative). Creates the Nebraska Apiary Advisory Board, composed of the Director and additional members appointed by the Director (including at least one commercial beekeeper, one hobbyist/sideliner, and one beekeeper active in a beekeeping organization); the Director serves as chair and fills vacancies. The Director may invite (but not require) a University of Nebraska entomology/apiculture representative to join. Board members serve without compensation but are eligible for expense reimbursement under sections 81-1174 to 81-1177. No explicit changes to Department funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included in the bill.
Additions: Creates a Nebraska Apiary Advisory Board within the Department of Agriculture. The Department director appoints and chairs the board, selecting at least one commercial beekeeper, one beekeeper active in a club, and one hobby/sideliner beekeeper; may invite (nonrequired) a UN entomology/apiculture re… 
Creates a Nebraska Apiary Advisory Board within the Department of Agriculture. The Department director appoints and chairs the board, selecting at least one commercial beekeeper, one beekeeper active in a club, and one hobby/sideliner beekeeper; may invite (nonrequired) a UN entomology/apiculture representative. Appointees serve without pay but may receive expense reimbursement under state travel statutes. The board will identify research gaps, recommend prevention/recovery actions for bee losses, assess impacts on Nebraska food systems, develop public education strategies, and work with the Legislature. Separately, the Board of Regents must create a full-time University of Nebraska–Lincoln extension educator with apiculture expertise. No explicit appropriations or budget allocations are included.

Summary: The bill requires the Secretary of State (SOS) to contract with the Department of Administrative Services for storage and distribution of official voter‑registration forms. SOS must provide the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) with instructions and materials on voter‑ID requirements and how to obtain free photographic ID; the DMV will make the voter registration application available at its offices and must complete applications taken there by… 
The bill requires the Secretary of State (SOS) to contract with the Department of Administrative Services for storage and distribution of official voter‑registration forms. SOS must provide the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) with instructions and materials on voter‑ID requirements and how to obtain free photographic ID; the DMV will make the voter registration application available at its offices and must complete applications taken there by close of business on the third Friday before an election. The DMV and SOS must enter an agreement to match the statewide voter registration list with DMV records (including citizenship) to verify registrations; the DMV director must also contract with the Social Security Commissioner. DMV and SOS must electronically transmit registration data to county election officials (generally within 10 days, five days near deadlines). Proceeds from sale of registration applications are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Election Administration Fund.
Additions: No provisions affect the Department of Administrative Services or the Department of Motor Vehicles, and there are no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text. LB544 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-601 (Employment Security Law). LB546 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-829.40 to clarify gubernatorial authority over emergencies and the Nebraska Emergency Management Agency (NEMA). The bill affirms the Governor’s responsibility for emergency management, authorizes assuming direct operational control of emergency functions, issuing state-of-emergency proclamations, and filing those proclamations with NEMA, the Secretary of State, and local government clerks. Proclamations activate state, city, village, county, and interjurisdictional emergency management organizations and authorize deployment of forces, supplies, and facilities. During an emergency the Governor is commander in chief of the organized and unorganized militia and other forces; the Governor may suspend regulatory statutes and utilize state and political-subdivision resources. The Legislature may terminate a proclamation. The original section is repealed and the act takes effect immediately. No funding or appropriation changes are included.

LB549 authorizes local school boards to employ (including volunteer) chaplains without a Nebraska teaching/admin certificate. Key government roles and changes:

- Commissioner of Education: may order criminal-history checks, and may deny a chaplain’s eligibility based on felony or certain misdemeanor convictions; notification/eligibility rules apply.
- Nebraska State Patrol: conducts fingerprinting and national criminal history checks at the commissioner's request and reports results to the commissioner.
- State Department of Education: retains existing personnel reporting framework (annual fall personnel report); chaplains are exempted from certificate registration requirements.
- County treasurer and school-board liability provisions that permit withholding of funds or personal liability for employing uncertified teachers/administrators are amended so they do not apply to chaplains.
- Applicants bear the actual direct costs of required background checks (per statute).

Summary: LB550 requires public school districts to adopt a released‑time policy excusing students to attend off‑campus religious instruction under specified conditions. Key provisions affecting government entities: - School districts must treat excused students as attending for purposes of school funding and attendance counts. - Released‑time courses generally may not be held on district property unless allowed under a neutral equal‑access policy that ope… 
LB550 requires public school districts to adopt a released‑time policy excusing students to attend off‑campus religious instruction under specified conditions. Key provisions affecting government entities:
- School districts must treat excused students as attending for purposes of school funding and attendance counts.
- Released‑time courses generally may not be held on district property unless allowed under a neutral equal‑access policy that opens facilities to community groups.
- Districts may award academic credit for such courses only after secular evaluation using the same criteria as similar offerings; credit determinations must be neutral to religious content or denomination.
- Districts may not deny released‑time sponsors equal access to funds, benefits, or services available to community groups.
- Aggrieved persons/organizations may sue districts for damages, equitable/declaratory relief, and attorney fees.
The act takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
Additions: Adds rules for "released time" courses administered around school districts: students excused to attend such courses are still considered enrolled in their school for attendance and school funding calculations; courses generally may not be held on district property unless allowed under a neutral equ… 
Adds rules for "released time" courses administered around school districts: students excused to attend such courses are still considered enrolled in their school for attendance and school funding calculations; courses generally may not be held on district property unless allowed under a neutral equal‑access policy; districts may award academic credit using secular, neutral evaluation criteria; districts cannot deny released‑time providers equal access to funds, benefits, or services they provide to other community groups. Enforcement allows private suits against the school district for actual damages, equitable/declaratory relief, and reasonable attorney fees. No state agency or department is named and there are no new appropriations or explicit budget allocations.

LB552 prohibits public postsecondary educational institutions governed by the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska, the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges, and community college governing boards from maintaining a “diversity, equity, and inclusion” (DEI) office or requiring or spending public money on DEI programs as defined in the bill. The measure defines prohibited activities (hiring influence, differential treatment, race-/gender‑referenced policies/programs) and allows exceptions: sexual‑harassment training; attorney‑staffed compliance offices; grant/accreditation statements highlighting first‑generation, low‑income, or underserved student support or certifying nondiscrimination; demographic data collection; scholarly research/art; recognized student organization activities; and short‑term guest speakers. Employees compelled to attend DEI programs may sue for injunctive relief. No new appropriations or positive budget allocations are included; the bill restricts use of public funds for DEI.

Adds definitions and restrictions applying to public postsecondary institutions governed by the Board of Regents (University of Nebraska), the Board of Trustees (Nebraska State Colleges), and community college governing boards. Defines "diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) office" and "DEI program" broadly to include units or trainings that influence hiring, provide differential treatment, implement race/gender‑referenced policies, or require employee participation. Prohibits requiring DEI participation as a condition of enrollment or institutional functions and bars spending public money on DEI programs or offices. Carves out exceptions (e.g., sexual‑harassment training; legal compliance offices staffed by attorneys; grant/accreditation statements; demographic data collection; scholarly research; student organization activities; short‑term guest speakers). Allows employees compelled to attend a DEI program to sue the institution for injunctive relief. No specific new appropriations or budget allocations are made; the change limits use of public funds for DEI.

LB555 amends the Funeral Directing and Embalming Practice Act to create a credentialed assistant funeral director role. Assistants may perform principal funeral-directing functions (management, services, burial arrangements, family coordination) only under the supervision and control of a licensed funeral director; embalming is expressly prohibited and violation requires immediate termination of the collaborative agreement and employment. Licensed funeral directors must execute, supervise, and retain records of a collaborative agreement with each assistant. The bill amends disciplinary authority (section 38-1424) to include failure to comply with the collaborative-agreement requirement and references enforcement under existing statutory procedures (section 38-196) and rules of "the department or other body having regulatory powers." The act repeals original sections and takes effect upon enactment. No appropriations or funding changes are included.

- Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): Peace officers who take juveniles into temporary custody under certain statutory subsections must deliver custody to DHHS for temporary placement in the least restrictive environment; DHHS will supervise placement and may consent to emergency medical, psychological, or psychiatric treatment. DHHS has no further authority absent a court order; its temporary custody terminates if no court order is issued within 48 hours. For juveniles believed to be mentally ill and dangerous, officers may place the juvenile at a mental health facility or deliver to DHHS and must execute and forward a prescribed written certificate to the county attorney.

LB557 amends multiple education statutes. Key agencies/departments and fiscal changes:

- State Department of Education (NDE): will certify school-building percentages qualifying for free/reduced meals (including a 1.6 multiplier for community eligibility) and reimburse resident districts for transportation of option students with disabilities per §79-1144.

- Commissioner of Education: prescribes option application/withdrawal forms; option districts must notify applicants within ten days.  
- School boards: must adopt and publish student-fee policies; may collect fees including transportation per §§79-605/79-611.  
- Learning community coordinating council: retained levy and fund-administration authorities (including focus program capital, early childhood, and other specified expenditures) and must administer learning community funds (§79-2111).  
- Funding/appropriations: parents of students denied option enrollment become eligible for a $2,500 educational support payment; net option funding formula revised to include converted contract option students and, from FY2023-24, equals net option count × (statewide average basic funding per formula student minus foundation aid). Payments for earlier years referenced to funds under §79-1005.01 and count as a formula resource.

Prohibits use of residential address, district capacity measures, or any measures that dis… 
Adds that option-enrollment applications may be submitted at any time and requires district selection standards to be limited to a random selection process and the interests of the student and parent/guardian. Prohibits use of residential address, district capacity measures, or any measures that discriminate by race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status or other protected classes. Establishes a process reference for requesting an "educational support payment" and makes a parent/guardian whose option-enrollment application is rejected eligible for a $2,500 payment for the applicable school year. Defines "student who contributes to the socioeconomic diversity of enrollment" using free/reduced-price lunch certifications pursuant to section 79-2120 and the community eligibility provision. Mentions school districts and learning communities and cites section 79-769.

LB559 creates new financial-crime offenses (skimmer installation/use; continuing criminal enterprise for financial transaction offenses) and expands forfeiture authority for covered offenses to include equipment, components, peripherals, software, hardware, accessories related to electronic communication devices. Procedural changes require the prosecuting authority to specifically plead forfeiture in the criminal information and authorize district-court pretrial and post‑conviction forfeiture hearings and intervention by third‑party claimants.

Fiscal/program provisions: the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund is created and administered by the Attorney General, funded by assets forfeited from financial transaction offenses. The State Investment Officer invests fund assets under existing state investment statutes. The Attorney General prescribes application processes, determines qualifying victim reimbursements (pro rata if insufficient funds), and holds funds for at least 36 months; thereafter remaining amounts are remitted to the State Treasurer for constitutionally directed distribution. No direct appropriation or budget allocation is specified.
Additions: Creates the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund, to be administered by the Nebraska Attorney General. Creates the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund, to be administered by the Nebraska Attorney General. The fund is to consist of assets forfeited from "financial transaction offenses" (per section 28-1601). The state investment officer will invest any available funds pursuant to the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The Attorney General will set application procedures, determine qualifying losses, and distribute reimbursements (pro rata if claims exceed available funds). Funds transferred into the fund remain there until the later of 36 months after transfer or resolution of applications filed in that period; thereafter remaining amounts are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, section 5 of the Nebraska Constitution. No specific appropriation amounts are provided.

LB560 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-3725 to revise the tourism grant programs administered by "the commission" and its executive director. Summary: The bill assigns responsibilities to the Department of Transportation (defined as “department”) related to special permits and overweight raw‑milk vehicle permits. The bill assigns responsibilities to the Department of Transportation (defined as “department”) related to special permits and overweight raw‑milk vehicle permits. The department (along with the Nebraska State Patrol and local authorities) may issue, condition, limit, or revoke permits, adopt rules, require security to cover roadway damage, and must make certain permit applications available in each county treasurer’s office. For overweight raw‑milk vehicles the department must create (by Jan. 1, 2026), annually review, and publish a bridge map identifying prohibited bridge structures. The department may revoke individual or all overweight raw‑milk permits if federal aid risk exists. The department may sue to recover bridge‑repair costs; recovered funds are credited to the Roads Operations Cash Fund.
Additions: The added provisions charge the Department of Transportation with establishing and managing an "overweight raw‑milk vehicle" program. Key DOT duties: define and issue/ revoke permits; by Jan 1, 2026 create a statewide "bridge map" of prohibited bridges, review it annually, and publish it online; aut… 
The added provisions charge the Department of Transportation with establishing and managing an "overweight raw‑milk vehicle" program. Key DOT duties: define and issue/ revoke permits; by Jan 1, 2026 create a statewide "bridge map" of prohibited bridges, review it annually, and publish it online; authorize interstate travel only with FHWA approval; grant limited vehicle‑length exceptions to meet axle weight limits; and revoke individual or all permits if federal aid is jeopardized. Operational limits: gross weight cap 107,500 lbs and axle loads per the federal bridge formula; permit holders must carry the bridge map and avoid prohibited structures. DOT may pursue owners for repair costs when prohibited bridges are damaged; recovered sums are credited to the Roads Operations Cash Fund. Revocation notices and appeals follow APA procedures.

LB562 amends statutes administered primarily by the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission and touches the Director of Motor Vehicles and county treasurers. Key agency provisions and fiscal changes:

- Game and Parks Commission: sets maximum fees for vehicle area permits (resident annual ≤ $50; nonresident = 2× resident; resident temporary ≤ $10; active-duty permit $5; disabled‑veteran permits free and perpetual). Commission may offer reduced-rate combinations and adopt rules.

- Mountain sheep permits: resident application fee ≤ $34; no more than two additional auction permits; auction revenues restricted to mountain sheep/elk/deer management.
- Limited landowner permits: deer/antelope limited permits = ½ regular fee (resident and nonresident structures); limited elk resident ≤ ½ regular, nonresident ≤ 3× resident; pre-season landowner permits (up to eight) cost $5 each.

LB565 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §84-901.03 (Administrative Procedure Act) to impose new requirements on state agencies regarding guidance documents. Agencies must post guidance at one public location and on their website, publish an annual index of applicable rules/guidance and submit it to the Clerk of the Legislature by Dec. 31, and place on each guidance’s first page a prescribed notice and an estimated fiscal-impact description covering state agencies, political subdivisions, and regulated entities. Agencies must respond within 60 days to written requests to revise, repeal, or convert guidance into rules and publicly post those decisions. The bill bars issuance of new guidance from July 1, 2025, to July 1, 2027, except for federal compliance, prevents guidance from exceeding federal requirements, and revokes guidance/provider bulletins dated July 1, 2022–July 1, 2025 pending rulemaking unless federally required. Emergency clause makes it effective on passage. No funding or appropriations are included.
Additions: Requires agencies to include an estimated fiscal-impact description for state agencies, political subdivisions, and regulated persons/businesses. Prohibits any agency from issuing guidance documents between July 1, 2025 and July 1, 2027 unless needed to comply with new or amended federal rules. Mand… 
Requires agencies to include an estimated fiscal-impact description for state agencies, political subdivisions, and regulated persons/businesses. Prohibits any agency from issuing guidance documents between July 1, 2025 and July 1, 2027 unless needed to comply with new or amended federal rules. Mandates that guidance may not impose stricter requirements on Nebraska residents or businesses than federal law. Revokes all guidance documents and provider bulletins issued July 1, 2022–July 1, 2025 pending formal rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act, except those explicitly required for federal compliance. No funding or appropriation changes are included.

LB572 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act to allow school districts to exceed their general‑fund budget authority to cover stipends paid to student teachers or interns (as defined in §79‑875) completing supervised teaching practicums in Nebraska public or private schools (adds new exclusion in §79‑1028.01). Summary: LB573 creates the Meat and Poultry Workers and Contractors Protection Act. It tasks "the commissioner" with receiving and investigating complaints, developing a compliance-monitoring process within 90 days, enforcing worker protections (including requiring covered employers to notify employees of collective-bargaining rights), and assessing civil penalties up to $15,000 for violations or anti-union misconduct. LB573 creates the Meat and Poultry Workers and Contractors Protection Act. It tasks "the commissioner" with receiving and investigating complaints, developing a compliance-monitoring process within 90 days, enforcing worker protections (including requiring covered employers to notify employees of collective-bargaining rights), and assessing civil penalties up to $15,000 for violations or anti-union misconduct. The bill references enforcement inadequacies by the federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration and invokes the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act for disaster-related injuries. The commissioner may bring civil actions and plaintiffs may sue employers for damages and liquidated damages. It also establishes a Workers and Contractors Task Force (includes two nonvoting legislative Agriculture Committee members) to report annually to the commissioner and Legislature. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
Additions: Creates new enforcement and oversight duties for "the commissioner" (state enforcement official): requiring covered industrial operators to file disaster mitigation plans; monitoring compliance (process due within 90 days); receiving, investigating, resolving complaints; assessing civil penalties up… 
Creates new enforcement and oversight duties for "the commissioner" (state enforcement official): requiring covered industrial operators to file disaster mitigation plans; monitoring compliance (process due within 90 days); receiving, investigating, resolving complaints; assessing civil penalties up to $15,000 for violations; and bringing civil actions on behalf of workers. The commissioner must also require employers (25+ employees) to provide workers information on federal collective-bargaining and FLSA rights. The bill establishes a Workers and Contractors Task Force appointed by the commissioner (includes two nonvoting members from the Legislature's Agriculture Committee) to meet quarterly, hold three regional stakeholder meetings annually, and submit an annual report to the commissioner and Legislature. Federal OSHA and the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act are referenced. No new state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.

Summary: LB574 sets procedural and employment protections for certified firefighters and emergency personnel. It requires fire department commanding officers to complete formal investigations within a reasonable timeframe, provide written complaint summaries before interviews, audio‑record interviews, and send written investigation outcomes. Complaints, statements, and recordings remain confidential unless law requires disclosure or the firefighter consen… 
LB574 sets procedural and employment protections for certified firefighters and emergency personnel. It requires fire department commanding officers to complete formal investigations within a reasonable timeframe, provide written complaint summaries before interviews, audio‑record interviews, and send written investigation outcomes. Complaints, statements, and recordings remain confidential unless law requires disclosure or the firefighter consents. Firefighters may have legal or union representation at hearings, cannot be compelled to take a polygraph, may seek damages (including attorney fees) for false complaints, and may challenge discipline via grievance or legal channels. The bill also affirms access to safe working conditions, training, equipment, mental‑health services, and personnel/training records, and allows off‑duty political activity. No state agencies, appropriations, or funding changes are specified.
Additions: Adds comprehensive procedural protections and workplace rights for firefighters: definitions; limits and timing for formal investigations; requirement to provide written complaint summaries before interviews; audio-recording of interviews; right to legal or union representation; written notice of ou… 
Adds comprehensive procedural protections and workplace rights for firefighters: definitions; limits and timing for formal investigations; requirement to provide written complaint summaries before interviews; audio-recording of interviews; right to legal or union representation; written notice of outcomes; confidentiality of complaints/records (unless law or consent requires disclosure); remedies for false complaints including attorney fees; access to grievance procedures; prohibition on compelled polygraph exams; rights to safe conditions, training, equipment, mental‑health services, off‑duty political activity, and access to personnel/training records. No specific government agencies or departments are named and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.

LB575 amends procedures under the Property Tax Request Act (section 77‑1633) and property tax levy limits (section 77‑3442). Key agency duties and fiscal effects:

- County clerks must organize a joint public hearing (held 7:00 p.m., on/after July 14 and before July 24) for political subdivisions seeking increases above allowable growth; county clerks must notify county assessors and participants by July 4. Political subdivisions must electronically send required information to county assessors by July 4. Postcards with tax estimates must be printed and initially paid from the county general fund and mailed at least seven days before the hearing; mailing costs are later charged proportionately to participating subdivisions based on parcel counts.

- Adds a new statutory levy constraint: when a political subdivision’s total taxable valuation rises, its levy is limited to the rate that would raise the identical dollar amount of property tax as the prior year; exceeding that limit requires a two‑thirds affirmative vote of the governing body.

- References affected: county assessor, county clerk, county board, county general fund, Department of Natural Resources, Division of Aeronautics (Dept. of Transportation), school districts, community colleges, natural resources districts, educational service units, regional metropolitan transit authority.
Additions: Adds subsection (12), which limits property tax levies for political subdivisions: if a political subdivision's total taxable valuation rises year‑to‑year, its levy may not be increased beyond the amount needed to raise the identical dollar amount of property tax revenue as the prior year. An overri… 
Adds subsection (12), which limits property tax levies for political subdivisions: if a political subdivision's total taxable valuation rises year‑to‑year, its levy may not be increased beyond the amount needed to raise the identical dollar amount of property tax revenue as the prior year. An override is allowed only by an affirmative two‑thirds vote of the subdivision's governing body. The provision is subject to an exception in section 77‑3444. No specific state agencies or departments are named, and there are no direct appropriations or line‑item funding changes; the change constrains local governments' ability to increase property tax revenue when valuations grow.

Summary: The bill assigns the Department of Revenue responsibility to determine the annual prepaid wireless surcharge, effective January 1, using the charge components in subsection (2) as of the preceding July 1. The bill assigns the Department of Revenue responsibility to determine the annual prepaid wireless surcharge, effective January 1, using the charge components in subsection (2) as of the preceding July 1. The department must post at least 90 days' advance notice of any surcharge change on its website. The prepaid rate is computed as the sum of three percentage components (the wireless E‑911 surcharge divided by 50; the Telecommunications Relay System Fund surcharge divided by 50; and the Universal Service Fund surcharge adjusted by the FCC safe‑harbor), rounded up to the nearest tenth of one percent. The Department must provide prepaid surcharge calculation and collection data to the Public Service Commission upon request. No appropriations or funding changes for the Department are included.

Summary: LB577 amends statutes administered by the Department of Health and Human Services concerning licensure and operations of remote dispensing pharmacies. Key changes: supervisory pharmacists must be licensed and located in Nebraska and supervise remote dispensing via a working real‑time audiovisual system; if the system fails, remote dispensing must stop. A remote dispensing pharmacy must share the same pharmacist‑in‑charge as its supervising pharma… 
LB577 amends statutes administered by the Department of Health and Human Services concerning licensure and operations of remote dispensing pharmacies. Key changes: supervisory pharmacists must be licensed and located in Nebraska and supervise remote dispensing via a working real‑time audiovisual system; if the system fails, remote dispensing must stop. A remote dispensing pharmacy must share the same pharmacist‑in‑charge as its supervising pharmacy, who must ensure a pharmacist is onsite at the remote location at least once per calendar month. The supervising pharmacist (or delegated pharmacist employed by the supervising pharmacy) retains responsibility for drug utilization review, final verification, and remote supervision. Supervising pharmacists must attempt patient counseling on all new prescriptions dispensed remotely. The bill repeals the original sections; no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
Additions: No underlined (added) text found in this bill. 
No underlined (added) text found in this bill.

Summary: - Requires the Department of Correctional Services (DCS) to pay committed offenders wages at least equal to the Wage and Hour Act, open deposit accounts for wage-earning offenders, and return/control earned funds at release (minimum one-third paid at release; full payment within six months). - Directs the DCS director to promulgate rules on hours, labor conditions, compensation, due process, and restitution collection; authorizes withholding/tran… 
- Requires the Department of Correctional Services (DCS) to pay committed offenders wages at least equal to the Wage and Hour Act, open deposit accounts for wage-earning offenders, and return/control earned funds at release (minimum one-third paid at release; full payment within six months).
- Directs the DCS director to promulgate rules on hours, labor conditions, compensation, due process, and restitution collection; authorizes withholding/transfers to satisfy restitution and requires an annual legislative report (number of inmates with restitution judgments, average payments, total collected).
- Requires DCS to act in accordance with the federal Occupational Safety and Health Act.
- Creates/clarifies the Reentry Cash Fund administered by DCS (funded by remittances under §33-157 and donations) to pay tuition, fees, and other reentry program costs for offenders in work camps.
- §33-157 directs initial transfers from the Nebraska Crime Victim Fund to the DCS Facility Cash Fund to cover LB510 implementation costs as certified by DCS.
- Defines occupational classification using the U.S. Department of Labor’s Dictionary of Occupational Titles.
Additions: - Department of Labor (Wage and Hour Act): The bill extends Wage and Hour Act wage protections to inmates and committed offenders—requiring wages "equal to or greater than" statutory levels—and explicitly includes the State and its political subdivisions (including inmates employed by the Department… 
- Department of Labor (Wage and Hour Act): The bill extends Wage and Hour Act wage protections to inmates and committed offenders—requiring wages "equal to or greater than" statutory levels—and explicitly includes the State and its political subdivisions (including inmates employed by the Department of Correctional Services or jails) within the employer definition.  
- Department of Correctional Services: The department must open deposit accounts for committed offenders earning wages (per section 83-183.01), give inmates control of those accounts, ensure inmate wages meet Wage and Hour Act standards, and comply with federal Occupational Safety and Health Act requirements for inmate employment. The Jail Standards Board will adopt rules on labor conditions, restitution transfers, and annual restitution reporting; administrators must provide data to support those reports.

No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.

LB579 amends Nebraska’s public records statutes to (1) prohibit custodians — including state agencies, counties, cities, villages, political subdivisions, and other public bodies or officials — from charging fees for public-record requests made by members of the Legislature, and (2) require custodians to respond within four business days after receipt with either access/copies (or an estimate of costs), a written denial with required information, or a written explanation including the earliest practicable fulfillment date for complex requests. State agencies providing records via the electronic portal established under section 84-1204 must obtain approval of proposed fees under sections 84-1205.02 and 84-1205.03. The bill repeals the prior versions of sections 84-712 and 84-712.01. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are made.

LB582 amends the Mechanical Amusement Device Tax Act and the Nebraska Tourism Commission fund statute. Beginning July 1, 2025, the Department (via the Tax Commissioner) will collect a 15% tax on net operating revenue of each cash device, remitted quarterly (Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1). The Tax Commissioner forwards receipts to the State Treasurer for credit as follows: 5% to the Charitable Gaming Operations Fund; 2.5% to the Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund; 20% to the General Fund; 47.5% to the Education Future Fund; 17.5% to the Property Tax Credit Cash Fund; and the remaining 7.5% to the county treasurer (distributed to county and/or city/village as specified). Exemptions include certain fraternal benefit societies and recognized veterans organizations. Section 81-3729 is amended to credit vendor/retailer and advertising revenue to the Nebraska Tourism Commission Promotional Cash Fund; the state investment officer may invest fund balances. Operative October 1, 2025.

Summary: LB583 assigns responsibilities and funding flows among named agencies: - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): will administer the Child Care Grant Fund and award grants (up to $15,000; one award per recipient every two years) to licensed child‑care providers, community organizations, or schools; DHHS may contract with a statewide organization to manage applications, review, and technical assistance. LB583 assigns responsibilities and funding flows among named agencies:

- Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): will administer the Child Care Grant Fund and award grants (up to $15,000; one award per recipient every two years) to licensed child‑care providers, community organizations, or schools; DHHS may contract with a statewide organization to manage applications, review, and technical assistance. DHHS also holds the Medicaid Fraud Settlement Fund from which 25% of the state portion (and separately 5% per the documentary stamp tax) is directed to the Health Care Homes for the Medically Underserved Fund for distribution to federally qualified health centers.

- Department of Veterans' Affairs: will administer the Military Installation Development and Support Fund (funded in part via section 76-903 revenues), with at least $100,000/year to the department for a statewide SkillBridge strategy and at least $100,000/year to veteran mental‑health community providers; project expenditures require a public/private match ≥50%.

- Department of Economic Development: will administer the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (receives funds from section 76-903) and may prioritize Economic Recovery Contingency Fund projects per the 2023 coordination plan.

- Department of Revenue: the Tax Commissioner (Dept. of Revenue) designs documentary stamps and may issue declaratory rulings; the department may not overturn county assessor sale‑qualification decisions without its own review.

- Military Department: included in the statutory definition of "military installation."

- Documentary stamp tax allocations (per $3.30 collected): $1.05 Affordable Housing; $0.25 Site & Building; $0.25 Homeless Shelter; $0.40 Behavioral Health; $0.05 Economic Recovery Contingency (for a grant‑coordination office); $0.05 Military Installation Development and Support; $0.05 Innovation Hub Cash Fund; $0.05 Health Care Homes; $0.40 Child Care Grant Fund; county retention $0.75. 

- Economic Recovery Contingency Fund transfers: specified transfers to the Museum Construction and Maintenance Fund ($750,000 in 2024; $15,000,000 in 2025; $7,000,000 in early 2026) and a $30,000,000 transfer to the Inland Port Authority Fund (and transfer of unobligated balances thereon July 31, 2026).
Additions: - Department of Economic Development: New allocation (5 cents per $1.05 transferred under section 76-903) funds an Economic Recovery Contingency Fund to establish/operate a statewide office to pursue and coordinate grant funding; Innovation Hub Cash Fund receives 5 cents per $1.05 for operational su… 
- Department of Economic Development: New allocation (5 cents per $1.05 transferred under section 76-903) funds an Economic Recovery Contingency Fund to establish/operate a statewide office to pursue and coordinate grant funding; Innovation Hub Cash Fund receives 5 cents per $1.05 for operational support of innovation hubs.

- Department of Health and Human Services: Child Care Grant Fund expanded to fund licensed child-care providers for staff retention/recruitment incentives and capital expenses; grants awarded by need, administered via a contracted statewide organization providing application processing and technical assistance. Behavioral Health Services Fund receives 40 cents per $1.05; Health Care Homes for the Medically Underserved Fund also receives transfers.

- Department of Revenue: No direct program changes noted; role limited to transfers under section 76-903.

- Department of Veterans' Affairs: Receives at least $100,000/year to contract with community organizations to create a statewide SkillBridge strategy/program to attract veterans.

- Military Department: Military Installation Development and Support Fund receives 5 cents per $1.05 to support community-based veteran services (per subsection 55-901).

LB585 amends the Community‑based Juvenile Services Aid Program administered by the commission, specifying budget set‑asides and programmatic partners. Two ten‑percent allocations of the annual General Fund appropriation (excluding administrative funds) are required: one ten percent for development/maintenance of a common data set and evaluation (with the University of Nebraska at Omaha, Juvenile Justice Institute, assisting in development, evaluation, logic models, and reporting) and a second ten percent for grants to community‑based organizations located in qualified census tracts with annual budgets ≤ $1 million focused on preventing juvenile crime prior to system involvement. Remaining funds are apportioned by commission rule via a formula based on residents ages 12–18 who come into contact with the juvenile justice system; the commission may require up to a 5% local match. The commission must consult with the Office of Probation Administration, juvenile diversion programs, courts, law enforcement, and the Nebraska Association of County Officials when adopting rules and reporting annually to the Governor and Legislature.

Adds a 10% set‑aside of the annual General Fund appropriation to the Community‑based Juvenile Services Aid Program (excluding administrative budget funds) for grants to community‑based organizations located in qualified census tracts (per 26 U.S.C. 42(d)(5)(B)(ii)(I), as of Jan 1, 2025) with budgets ≤ $1 million and focused on preventing juvenile crime before justice‑system contact. Distribution criteria must consider staff with lived juvenile‑justice experience, organization budget size, tract location, and served population demographics. The University of Nebraska at Omaha Juvenile Justice Institute will assist grantees in creating logic models and evaluation measures.

Summary: LB586 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §32‑944 to require county election officials, in coordination with county sheriffs, jail/detention center directors or designated staff, and election commissioners or county clerks, to develop and implement a written plan ensuring incarcerated or otherwise restricted individuals housed in county jails/detention centers can verify, change, or register to vote, return ballots (including a designated on‑site collection l… 
LB586 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §32‑944 to require county election officials, in coordination with county sheriffs, jail/detention center directors or designated staff, and election commissioners or county clerks, to develop and implement a written plan ensuring incarcerated or otherwise restricted individuals housed in county jails/detention centers can verify, change, or register to vote, return ballots (including a designated on‑site collection location and use of two registered voters of different party affiliation to collect ballots), and cure ballot deficiencies. Election commissioners or county clerks must adopt procedures conforming to the Election Act and rules promulgated by the Secretary of State. Noncompliance by sheriffs or facility directors/staff subjects the county to a civil penalty set by the district court. The bill repeals the original section. No appropriations or funding changes are specified.
Additions: Adds requirements for county jails/detention centers to provide restricted (incarcerated) individuals with information and reasonable access to verify, change, or register to vote; a designated on-site location for ballot return; instructions on return methods, location, and deadlines; and a process… 
Adds requirements for county jails/detention centers to provide restricted (incarcerated) individuals with information and reasonable access to verify, change, or register to vote; a designated on-site location for ballot return; instructions on return methods, location, and deadlines; and a process to cure ballot deficiencies. Ballots at facilities must be returned for collection by two registered voters who are not affiliated with the same political party. The county sheriff or facility director/designated staff must perform duties consistent with the Election Act. LB587 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act by revising sections 76-1425 and 76-1427. Key changes: tenants may terminate for landlord noncompliance with shorter notice for recurring breaches (now at least seven days' written notice for a repeat violation within six months); landlords have a seven-day cure period for material noncompliance before a termination date set not less than fourteen days after notice. Tenant remedies are expanded to explicitly include remediation of known mold problems and pest infestations (tenant may purchase supplies/services and deduct costs from rent), recovery for diminution in fair rental value, recovery for loss in value of the tenant's personal property, rent abatement for the period of noncompliance, and, for deliberate failures, recovery of actual/reasonable cost or fair value of substitute housing. Reasonable attorney’s fees are allowed. No state agencies, departments, or budget appropriations are referenced or affected.
Additions: Adds tenant remedies for landlord failure to remediate known mold or pest infestations: tenants may (a) purchase supplies or services to remediate during the landlord’s noncompliance and deduct actual, reasonable costs from rent, and (b) recover damages for diminution in value of the tenant’s person… 
Adds tenant remedies for landlord failure to remediate known mold or pest infestations: tenants may (a) purchase supplies or services to remediate during the landlord’s noncompliance and deduct actual, reasonable costs from rent, and (b) recover damages for diminution in value of the tenant’s personal property caused by the landlord’s deliberate or negligent noncompliance. Text also reorganizes/remarks subsections. No government agencies or funding/appropriations are mentioned or changed.

LB588 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-512. LB589 amends §79‑1142, affecting the State Board of Education, Department of Education, State Treasurer, Director of Administrative Services, Governor, and legislative Appropriations and Education Committees. Key agency/fiscal provisions:

- State Board sets the support‑services reimbursement cap (not to exceed 10% minus the Legislature‑set support services set‑aside).
- Department of Education reimburses school districts/cooperatives 80% of total allowable excess special‑education costs; if General Fund appropriations are insufficient, payments are pro rata from the General Fund and the remainder paid from the Education Future Fund.
- State Treasurer must notify the Director of Administrative Services monthly of available General Fund and Education Future Fund amounts; the director issues warrants.
- Residential placements reimbursed from appropriated set‑aside funds based on average per‑pupil cost; the department may audit claims and subtract erroneous payments.
- Payments schedule and timelines specified; Extraordinary Increase Act payments are subtracted and transferred to the Education Future Fund.
- Districts must provide four days of professional leave for special‑education staff with substitute coverage.
- Department must report totals to the Governor and legislative committees by Nov. 15 annually.

LB590 authorizes the Department of Transportation to, by rule and regulation, establish, use, and operate a mitigation bank or an in-lieu fee program in accordance with applicable state and federal law. The program is intended to provide compensatory mitigation for incidental take of threatened or endangered species and their habitat (restoring, creating, enhancing, preserving, or combinations thereof) and to achieve a net increase in conservation functions and values. Owners of such mitigation banks (state, local, or private) must pay a sum in lieu of ad valorem taxes to the county. The bill contains no appropriations or other changes to the Department of Transportation’s budget.

Authorizes the Department of Transportation to adopt rules and establish, use, and operate a mitigation bank or in‑lieu fee program under applicable state and federal law to provide compensatory mitigation for incidental take of threatened or endangered species and their habitat from permitted projects. The program’s purpose includes restoring/creating/enhancing/preserving habitat, using a fair and practicable acreage ratio to offset project impacts, and achieving a net increase in conservation functions and values for affected species and resources. Fiscal change: owners of mitigation banks (state, local, or private) that acquire land for habitat work must pay a sum in lieu of lost ad valorem county taxes. No explicit DOT appropriations or budget allocations are included.

LB591 amends the Nebraska Installment Loan Act to clarify licensure jurisdiction. It makes procurement of a license from "the department" the requirement for persons making installment loans and expands licensing to any nonfinancial person who, at or after a loan is made, markets, owns, holds, acquires, services, or otherwise engages in loan activity with an installment loan borrower. It creates an exemption allowing an affiliate to avoid licensing if its in‑state activities are limited solely to securitization and servicing rights remain with the licensee or are assigned to a financial institution, licensee, or permittee. The bill defines "affiliate" and "control" (including a 25% voting‑share threshold or control of director elections). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.

LB594 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-6,179.01 to prohibit physically holding or otherwise using a handheld wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle in motion. Explicit exemptions cover persons performing official duties as law enforcement officers, firefighters, ambulance drivers, or emergency medical technicians; employees/contractors of utility service providers responding to utility emergencies; and drivers in emergency situations communicating with emergency services. The bill allows device use without touching the device or to initiate a function with a single touch. Violations are traffic infractions, assessed license points under §60-4,182, and fined $200 (first), $300 (second), $500 (third+). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The original section is repealed.

Summary: LB597 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act and changes duties/timelines for the State Department of Education, the Property Tax Administrator, the Tax Commissioner, the Director of Administrative Services, the Auditor of Public Accounts, the Appropriations Committee, the Governor, the Education Committee, the State Board, and the Tax Equalization and Review Commission. Key agency-related changes: - Foundation aid: Dept… 
LB597 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act and changes duties/timelines for the State Department of Education, the Property Tax Administrator, the Tax Commissioner, the Director of Administrative Services, the Auditor of Public Accounts, the Appropriations Committee, the Governor, the Education Committee, the State Board, and the Tax Equalization and Review Commission.

Key agency-related changes:
- Foundation aid: Dept. of Education pays $1,500 per formula student through FY2024-25; beginning FY2025-26 each district receives the greater of $1,500 per student or 7.5% of basic funding. Twenty-four percent of foundation aid is paid from the Education Future Fund. Inclusion of foundation aid as a formula resource falls from 100% (FY2023-24 and FY2024-25) to 60% beginning FY2025-26.
- Local effort rate: beginning FY2025-26 the rate for certification is the maximum levy under §77-3442 less $0.10; yields computed using adjusted valuations.
- Adjusted valuations: county assessor certification by Aug. 20 (amendments by Aug. 31); Property Tax Administrator certifies adjusted valuations to the Dept. of Education by Oct. 10. Agricultural land adjusted valuation rate reduced from 72% to 65% beginning FY2025-26.
- Certification/budget dates: state aid, district budget authority, and allowable reserve percentages certified on or before June 15, 2025 and on or before March 1 each year thereafter; any certifications for FY2025-26 completed before the act’s effective date are null and void.
- Funding/appropriations: Dept. must report necessary funding levels to Governor and legislative committees; Appropriations Committee must include amounts necessary to fund certified state aid. The Director of Administrative Services issues warrants for lump-sum/state aid payments as directed.
Additions: Effective for school fiscal year 2025-26 and thereafter, the bill (1) sets a new foundation aid floor for each school district: the greater of $1,500 per formula student or 7.5% of basic funding (per §79‑1007.16); (2) changes how the local effort rate is set: for state aid certification (§79‑1022) i… 
Effective for school fiscal year 2025-26 and thereafter, the bill (1) sets a new foundation aid floor for each school district: the greater of $1,500 per formula student or 7.5% of basic funding (per §79‑1007.16); (2) changes how the local effort rate is set: for state aid certification (§79‑1022) it equals the maximum levy authorized under §77‑3442 minus $0.10, while for final state aid calculations (§79‑1065) it is the rate that, when applied to total adjusted valuation of local systems receiving equalization aid under the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act (TEEOSA), produces the shortfall that state appropriations by the Legislature plus other local receipts must cover; and (3) fixes adjusted valuation used for aid calculations at 65% of actual value and 65% of special valuation (per referenced §§77‑1359, 77‑1363, 77‑1343).

LB59 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §2-3224 governing natural resources districts. It authorizes district fund disbursements not only by written instruments signed by the treasurer (or an authorized signer) but also by electronic payment systems, explicitly including electronic funds transfers and automated clearinghouse transfers. The secretary must report newly filed or changed bonds at each board meeting. No appropriations or budgetary changes are included.

LB5 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-470 to provide immunity related to opioid antagonists. It shields health professionals licensed under the Uniform Credentialing Act (physicians, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, pharmacists) from administrative or criminal action when, with reasonable care, they prescribe, administer, or dispense opioid antagonists. Emergency responders licensed under the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act or via the EMS Licensure Interstate Compact and peace officers, as well as law enforcement employees, are protected from administrative action, criminal prosecution, and personal civil liability (except for willful, wanton, or grossly negligent acts) when they obtain and administer opioid antagonists from their EMS organization or law enforcement agency. Law enforcement agencies and EMS organizations remain potentially liable for their personnel’s acts. Defined agencies include police departments, town marshals, sheriffs’ offices, and the Nebraska State Patrol. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.

LB600 grants several powers and duties to the Department of Transportation (DOT). DOT (or its agents) may remove vehicles or other objects from highways or shoulders without owner consent and is immune from liability for damage. DOT may temporarily reduce maximum lawful speeds for specified conditions, must display electronic/digital signage when doing so, develop/implement policy for such reductions, keep records of changes and highway speed limits, and adopt rules to implement the process. DOT may enforce school-crossing and highway-work-zone speed limits using speed control enforcement systems and may contract with operators. DOT must create a guidance document to calculate administrative fees related to system-issued warnings/citations and must erect and maintain signage notifying motorists of the move-over requirement on controlled-access highways. Civil penalties collected are remitted to the State Treasurer. No appropriations or budget allocations are specified.

Adds authority and procedures for the Department of Transportation (DOT) to: remove vehicles/objects impeding traffic (with immunity from damage liability); temporarily lower posted highway speed limits for defined conditions (weather, traction, emergencies, congestion) using electronic/digital signage in 5 mph increments, with required policy, recordkeeping, and rulemaking; and enforce school-crossing and highway work-zone speed limits using speed control enforcement systems (automated devices), including contracting operators. Sets operation standards (active warning lights/workers present, signage), speed thresholds for automated citations (school: >6 mph; work zone: >11 mph), owner notice, appeal process, civil-penalty schedule, confidentiality and calibration/logging requirements, and guidance on administrative fees. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.

LB602 (the "Delete Act") assigns primary administrative authority to the Secretary of State and enforcement powers to the Attorney General. Key agency actions and fiscal provisions:

- Secretary of State: annual data-broker registration (by Jan 31) with required disclosures; registration fee set by the Secretary of State (not to exceed $300); must publish registration information and create an accessible statewide deletion mechanism by Jan 1, 2028; may charge data brokers an access fee limited to the Secretary of State’s reasonable costs; may adopt implementing rules. Secretary of State selects independent auditors for triennial audits (first by Dec 31, 2030) and receives audit reports on request.

- Financial penalties and fees: civil penalty of $200/day per uncompleted deletion request payable to the Secretary of State; the Attorney General may sue to collect penalties, seek injunctive relief, and recover attorneys’ fees and costs.

Adds roles for the Secretary of State and Attorney General. The Secretary of State must host data-broker registration info and create an accessible deletion mechanism by Jan 1, 2028, set a registration fee (up to $300) and may charge data brokers an access fee not to exceed the Secretary's reasonable costs, adopt rules, select independent auditors for triennial audits (first by Dec 31, 2030), receive audit reports on request, and require retention of audit materials for six years. Data brokers register annually (by Jan 31) and use the deletion mechanism beginning Aug 1, 2028. Noncompliance triggers civil penalties ($200/day per uncompleted deletion request) payable to the Secretary of State. The Attorney General may enforce the Act, collect penalties, seek injunctive relief, and recover attorney fees. No explicit new appropriations; fees and penalties are the identified funding flows.

109-1-LB604_IntroReferralLegislature 109, Session 1 (2025)LB604_Intro_Copy.docxDOCX
Summary: LB604 amends initiative and referendum procedures, assigning specific duties to state officers and clarifying judicial review.
